transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Carter (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Marta Ruiz (Lumina, Head Eng); Dan Cho (CTO); Evan Brooks (Security); Priya Nair (Product)

Summary:
Redwood walk-through focused on data handling and retention controls in the Console and API (logging redaction, PII handling, request storage toggles, and audit logs). Customer is evaluating options for hosted vs dedicated given PCI-esque constraints; main concerns are PII retention, logs for fraud investigation, and SOC2/SSO integration.

Topics:
- Data retention controls (request storage toggles, TTLs)
- Logging redaction and redaction rules (PII removal, regex patterns)
- Audit logs, KMS integration, and encryption in transit/at-rest
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for cost and isolation
- Pilot plan and benchmarks

[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, and we'll do a 30-ish minute walkthrough then q&a.
[00:18] Marta (Lumina): hi Sophie, thanks; we have a hard stop at 16:00 but should be fine.
[00:25] Ravi (Redwood SE): hi team, Ravi here — I'll drive the console demo, show toggles for request storage and redaction rules, and then we can dig into the Dedicated option.
[00:42] Dan (Lumina): great, thanks. high level: Lumina processes card-not-present transactions, so PII handling and short retention windows are critical. we also need logs for fraud investigations for up to 90 days.
[01:05] Evan (Lumina, Security): and we need to understand what we can redact vs what we must keep for e-discovery.
[01:20] Sophie: absolutely, that's what we'll focus on. quick context: Redwood supports hosted API with request-storage toggles, plus Dedicated for customer-isolated GPU pools. both can be configured with KMS and VPC peering for private deployments.
[01:45] Ravi: jumping into the Console — I'm sharing screen — ok you should see the Data Controls page. top-level toggle: 'Store requests' on/off per project, and a dropdown to auto-strip PII.
[02:12] Marta: can you show an example of a redaction rule?
[02:18] Ravi: yep. here's the default redaction preset: removes email-like patterns, credit-card-like patterns, and tokens matching SSN regex. it's a chain of rules so you can reorder and add custom regex. note: it's best-effort — we recommend client-side hashing for anything you absolutely must never send.
[02:45] Dan: when you say 'remove', do you mean full removal from logs or replacement with a placeholder? we need traceback for debugging but not raw PANs.
[03:05] Ravi: good question. by default we replace with placeholders like <REDACTED_EMAIL> or <REDACTED_CC4>. there's also an option to hash fields instead of removing, which preserves referential lookup for analytics but prevents seeing raw values.
[03:32] Evan: does hashing use customer KMS so we control keys?
[03:38] Ravi: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support BYOK via KMS/HSM — you can bring keys, and hashed values won't be reversible without the key. for hosted customers we offer managed keys but can do dedicated key stores for enterprise.
[03:58] Sophie: another knob is per-route storage policy. e.g., you might store embedding calls for 7 days while generation requests are off by default. you can set TTLs at the model route level.
[04:20] Priya (Lumina): is TTL enforced automatically or is it a retention policy we have to run deletion jobs for?
[04:34] Ravi: it's enforced by Redwood's control plane — once TTL expires records are purged from primary store and archival. we also provide retention-cert reports for audits.
[04:50] Dan: does purge include backups? we have to ensure deletion from snapshots for compliance.
[05:05] Ravi: yes — we have configurable backup retention windows and can tie purge to snapshot lifecycle so backups older than X are also removed. for Private deployments you can opt to manage backup lifecycle in your infra.
[05:25] Marta: about request-storage toggles — is that per env? like dev vs prod?
[05:35] Ravi: per-project and can be overridden per-route. common pattern: dev store everything, prod store minimal with redaction.
[05:48] Sophie: wanted to highlight the Request Audit view — you can search by hashed identifier, see who accessed a request, and export audit logs for SIEM ingestion.
[06:15] Evan: what's in the audit logs? does it include prompt text?
[06:22] Ravi: audit logs include metadata (timestamp, route, model, user id, redaction status, hashes) but don't include raw prompt unless storage was enabled for that route. so if you disable storage, the audit log will show the action occurred but not the content.
[06:48] Dan: ok that sounds promising. can we do selective capture? e.g., capture prompts for flagged transactions only?
[07:00] Ravi: yes — you can set capture rules based on attributes (like transaction risk score) and route those requests to a secure bucket with stricter retention, or send them to SIEM.
[07:22] Marta: for fraud investigations we need timeline reconstruction. hashing helps but sometimes we need to re-link conversations. any guidance?
[07:35] Sophie: many customers store a reversible token in a secure vault when they absolutely need to re-link, but that's a controlled flow requiring KMS and RBAC. we can document best practices.
[08:00] Dan: for PCI-adjacent data, are we talking about Dedicated only or can hosted be used?
[08:12] Ravi: hosted can be used if you don't store PAN and you meet network isolation requirements — but for stronger isolation Dedicated or Private is recommended. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, dedicated network egress, and fine-grained key control.
[08:33] Evan: what's the latency/cost delta? we want to know impacts for real-time fraud scoring.
[08:45] Ravi: Dedicated typically reduces noisy neighbors and gives more predictable latency — cost is higher due to reserved capacity. we can run a benchmark during the pilot and share per-token cost estimates with batching configs.
[09:10] Priya: can you demo the API toggle for request-storage? we want to flip it via infra as code.
[09:20] Ravi: yep — here's the API route: PATCH /projects/{id}/routes/{route_id} with storage.enabled = false and redaction.preset = "strict". we have Terraform provider as well.
[09:45] Dan: perfect. any chance of a quick demo of redaction misfires — false negatives? how do we validate?
[09:58] Ravi: there's a Redaction Preview tool — you paste sample text and it shows matched rules and the transformed output. it's not a silver bullet; we recommend evaluator tests and sample-driven evals — Redwood Optimize can run regression checks over prompt sets to detect redaction regressions.
[10:30] Marta: that could be useful — we have a set of prompt families to test.
[10:36] Sophie: we'd like to run those as part of the pilot, include a few regression alerts.
[10:45] Evan: on encryption — can you outline at-rest and in-transit details briefly?
[10:52] Ravi: in-transit: TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS option for Private; at-rest: data is encrypted with AES-256, key management via customer KMS for Dedicated/Private. Logs and backups can be segregated per project and encrypted with separate keys.
[11:15] Dan: good. for audit we need SOC2 and penetration test reports.
[11:22] Sophie: we'll send SOC2 and recent pentest summary in the follow-up.
[11:28] Priya: about e-discovery — can Redwood support export of stored requests in a compliant format?
[11:36] Ravi: yes — exports come as timestamped JSON bundles with hashes and metadata; we can ship via SFTP or to an S3 bucket with presigned access.
[11:52] Marta: do you log model outputs? sometimes model hallucinations are a risk for compliance.
[11:59] Ravi: outputs are subject to same storage toggles — by default outputs are off for prod routes, but you can enable for flagged cases. we also support output fingerprinting (hash+schema) for quick dedup/lookup.
[12:20] Dan: what about retention certifications? we need attestations for regulators that data was purged.
[12:30] Ravi: we provide retention-cert proofs — a signed record showing deletion timestamps and scope. for Dedicated we can provide audit log exports corroborating the purge.
[12:50] Evan: are there any compliance customers in payments you can reference?
[12:58] Sophie: we've had a few mid-market payment customers running pilots; i can share redacted case studies and customer references in the follow-up.
[13:10] Priya: can you show the UI flow for setting redaction rules and route TTL?
[13:20] Ravi: sure — going to the Route config — TTL set to 7 days, override to 0 for no storage. adding rule: name = 'card-mask', regex = '4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?' — that's for Visa-like PAN detection. note: we include checksum heuristics to reduce false positives.
[14:05] Marta: can the regex engine be sandboxed? we have security concerns about complex regex running in the control plane.
[14:15] Ravi: yes — we sandbox and limit execution time; complex transforms can be executed client-side or in a worker you host.
[14:30] Dan: what's the rollback story if purge runs and we need data for investigation?
[14:40] Ravi: purge is irreversible by default; backups are purged per retention lifecycle. we recommend a short quarantine window for high-risk items where you store a lookup token in a secure vault for a fixed period, with strict access controls and audit.
[15:05] Evan: do you support SSO/SAML + RBAC for accessing the Request Audit? we need least-privilege.
[15:14] Sophie: yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and customizable roles — you can restrict deletion and export privileges to a small set of admins.
[15:35] Priya: can we get a demo that shows the Request Audit search by hashed token?
[15:45] Ravi: switching to Audit screen — searching by hash now — you can see request metadata, route, model and redaction status. clicking into record shows redaction diff and export options if policy allows.
[16:10] Marta: the UI looks solid. how do we automate policy via IaC? you mentioned Terraform provider.
[16:20] Ravi: here's a sample HCL: redwood_route { storage = false; redaction_preset = "strict"; ttl_days = 7 } — it maps to the API. we also have a CLI for quick toggles.
[16:45] Dan: good. let's talk about pilot scope — we'd want to test real transaction streams and fraud scoring, maybe 2-4 models and different batch sizes.
[16:58] Sophie: recommended pilot: 2 weeks, compare hosted vs Dedicated for a subset of traffic; include redaction evals, latency benchmark, and cost estimates with Optimize recommendations.
[17:20] Evan: does Redwood Optimize suggest batching configs and quantization profiles? for inference cost/cpu footprint.
[17:28] Ravi: yes, Optimize will profile your workload and recommend batch sizes, kv cache settings, and quantization levels that balance latency vs cost; we can run that as part of pilot.
[17:50] Priya: are there any gotchas with embeddings and PII? we plan to embed transaction metadata.
[17:58] Ravi: embeddings can leak info if not redacted; you should strip PII before embedding or use a hashing layer. we also support dedup and prefix caching to reduce redundant embeddings storage.
[18:20] Dan: for the Dedicated pricing, do you have ballpark numbers?
[18:28] Sophie: we'll send a tailored estimate after we see the pilot metrics; reserved capacity pricing is monthly with tiered throughput.
[18:40] Marta: one more security question: do you maintain tenant separation at the data-layer in hosted?
[18:47] Ravi: logical separation with strict ACLs in hosted; Dedicated gives physical isolation at the compute and often storage layer. we can provide architecture diagrams.
[19:05] Dan: any limitations for region / data residency?
[19:12] Sophie: we have multi-region support; for strict residency you can use Private or deploy to a specific cloud region.
[19:25] Evan: okay — quick show of the redaction preview with a sample payload.
[19:32] Ravi: pasting sample: 'card=4111111111111111, email=marta@lumina.com, comment=customer says password is 1234' — preview shows card -> <REDACTED_CC>, email -> <REDACTED_EMAIL>, password -> <REDACTED>. note: password patterns need explicit rules; we can include a default 'sensitive keywords' list.
[20:05] Priya: what about false positives on card regexes — we sometimes have order numbers that start with 4.
[20:12] Ravi: the checksum plus context heuristics reduces that; also you can whitelist patterns to avoid false hits.
[20:30] Marta: let's talk about logs exported to SIEM — can we push to Splunk in near real-time?
[20:38] Ravi: yes — webhook or streaming export to external SIEMs; payloads are configurable and can exclude redacted fields.
[20:55] Dan: on RBAC again — can we restrict export capability to read-only auditor role?
[21:02] Sophie: absolutely, roles are fine-grained — we can demo SCIM role mappings in the pilot.
[21:20] Evan: for legal/ procurement — any standard contract addenda for data handling?
[21:28] Sophie: yes we have DPA templates and can negotiate specific clauses for retention and deletion. I'll loop legal after this call.
[21:40] Priya: timeline — we're aiming for pilot in next two weeks. is that realistic?
[21:47] Ravi: yes if you share PII list and sample traffic, we can spin up a Dedicated trial and run benchs.
[22:02] Marta: i'll share the PII list and success metrics today.
[22:10] Sophie: perfect — ok final demo bit: showing the retention-cert generation flow. clicking 'Generate Retention Cert' — select scope (project, route) — system compiles purge logs and signs the cert.
[22:35] Dan: wow, that's useful. is that tied to an audit event?
[22:40] Ravi: yes — cert references audit events and deletion timestamps; available for export.
[23:00] Priya: any developer ergonomics? SDKs for toggling storage and sampling?
[23:08] Ravi: SDKs for Python/JS/Go with helpers to mask client-side, and feature flags to toggle capture sampling.
[23:30] Marta: let's talk a bit about error cases — if redaction fails and PII gets stored, what's the incident response flow?
[23:40] Sophie: we have incident runbooks; for dedicated pilots we can commit to a notification SLA and remediation steps. legal will want documented commitments which we can discuss.
[24:00] Evan: one more: can we restrict engineer access to raw outputs except under a formal IR process?
[24:10] Ravi: yes, that's enforced through RBAC + approval workflow; exports require signed request and recorded justifications.
[24:30] Dan: good. anything on telemetry retention for Optimize? we don't want embedding or prompt telemetry to be retained longer than necessary.
[24:40] Ravi: Optimize can be run in an ephemeral mode where profiles are generated off ephemeral data, or you can supply anonymized metrics. There's a config to not persist raw prompts used in profiling.
[25:05] Priya: ok let's recap next steps.
[25:10] Sophie: recap: Sophie sends SOC2 and security materials; Ravi provisions Dedicated trial and sets up redaction and TTL templates; Lumina shares PII list and metrics; schedule pilot kickoff.
[25:25] Marta: yep. timeline: expecting pilot to start week of 2026-03-30.
[25:32] Dan: agreed.
[25:40] Evan: one question for follow-up: can Redwood run a small test that shows deletion from backups (we'll want a proof-of-delete)?
[25:50] Ravi: yes we can script a proof-of-delete as part of retention-cert generation.
[26:00] (cross-talk)
[26:10] Sophie: any last questions?
[26:18] Priya: none from product.
[26:22] Marta: no. thanks — we'll look out for materials.
[26:30] Sophie: thanks everyone. wrapping up in next steps and action items.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcription quality: automated transcript had a few mis-hearings — e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K-V cash'. Proper nouns like some customer internal tool names may be off.
